content:
maria: quick q — i'm about to land a TF change that flips a per-model feature flag via a ConfigMap. want to avoid full pod restarts for a hot toggle. current plan is to write a checksum annotation on the deployment so k8s rolls pods only when the flag changes. any caveats?

zach: that pattern (annotation with cm sha) is common. note: mounting a configmap as a file does NOT trigger a restart by itself. you need to change the pod template to force a rollout.

maria: yep exactly. terraform will compute sha256 of the rendered configmap and add annotation `configmap-checksum/model-config` on the deployment. example in my head: 

```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    configmap-checksum/model-config: "${data.template_file.model_config.rendered_sha}"
```

oliver: two quick gotchas: 1) ensure the TF data source is stable (ordering of keys) so the sha doesn't flip unnecessarily. 2) watch for large configmaps — terraform templating could hide diffs.

sasha: for the runtime, also consider using our KV prefix cache invalidation instead of pod rollouts when possible. if it's just runtime knobs read at request time, we can invalidate cache instead of restarting.

maria: good call. this is a per-model routing knob that the runtime reads on each request already, but we have some values that are only read at startup (buffer sizes). mixed.

jen: another option: expose the flags via API from config service and have pods poll/update in-memory. that avoids rollout churn, but adds code complexity.

infra-bot: deploy-check: remember to add rollout_timeout and max_unavailable in the deployment strategy to keep SLOs.

zach: if you go with the annotation approach, add a small smoke test that updates the CM and asserts one pod cycles and continues serving traffic. also add a sanity eval for the model route.

maria: draft PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/652 — changes: data.template_file for model config, deployment annotation, kube-deploy pipeline step to run smoke check.

oliver: i skimmed — lgtm but please add a short unit test for the template rendering (prevent key-order flaps). you can use the existing template_test harness under infra/tests.

sasha: +1 on tests. also add a note in the rollout playbook about how to revert quickly (kubectl rollout undo or reapply old annotation).

jen: for canary, we can route 5% of traffic to a Dedicated pool variant that has the startup-only buffer set, then bump. less risky than cluster-wide.

maria: will add tests + playbook entry + canary plan. i'll also add an explicit TF comment explaining stable ordering (+ sort_keys true in template helper). thanks all :thumbsup:

zach: one more: add a terraform output of the computed checksum so we can reference it in CI logs if needed. makes debugging easier.

maria: noted — adding output and a short CI step to echo it after apply. tagging @jen for rollout ops sync if anything else needed.

jen: i'll watch the canary next week, thx.

infra-bot: reminder: update CHANGELOG (infra) with the config rollout pattern and link to the playbook.
